title: [BUG] P0 Mac TTS runtime path missing — NotificationFired observer never calls AudioPlayer, no UNUserNotificationCenter in nexus-mac
description: ROOT CAUSE for 'no banner no audio' across the entire diagnostic arc 2026-05-19/20. The supersede-mac-tts-listener-spec narrative claimed Swift owns TTS end-to-end. In reality: (1) apps/swift/nexus-mac/Sources/AudioPlayer.swift exists but its ONLY caller is ElevenLabsSettingsView.swift:82 (test voice button). NO observer subscribes to NotificationFired events and calls play(). (2) UNUserNotificationCenter does NOT exist in nexus-mac target — only nexus-watch + nexus-ios. macOS literally cannot show a banner. (3) audioBase64 field is missing from Swift NotificationEvent — only referenced in test comments. (4) The Notifications HISTORY sidebar IS wired (consumeNotifications->prepend) which made it look like SSE worked. The TTS path is structurally absent. Required work: app-level @main observer that subscribes to /events/stream window-independently, calls a synthesis path (AVSpeechSynthesizer offline OR ElevenLabs HTTP if api key set), pipes mp3 bytes to AudioPlayer.shared.play, AND posts a UNMutableNotificationContent via UNUserNotificationCenter.current(). UNUserNotificationCenter needs permission flow + entitlement on first launch. Estimated: medium spec (8-15 tasks, primarily Swift).
notes: Resolution scope captured in spec mac-tts-runtime-wire-up (feature nx-kk2qa, 13 tasks under capability nx-ga815). When that spec applies, this bug is fixed.

title: Dashboard window never mounts SessionsView -> startStreams never fires -> zero fetch (client code bug)
description: ROOT CAUSE (runtime-proven 2026-05-19, after deploy/build/config all verified good): the nexus-mac app makes ZERO network connections and ZERO logs despite: fresh build from HEAD, nexus.dashboard.endpoint=http://100.73.182.4:7400 set in domain dev.leonardoacosta.nexus.mac, macbook->homelab HTTP 200, homelab serving 5 dashboard-visible sessions, resolveClients() provably non-empty (NexusAggregateClient.swift:63 localhost fallback). fetchSessions() is never invoked. startStreams() (SessionObserver.swift:48) has exactly one mac caller: SessionsView.swift:38 .task. So SessionsView.task never fires => the dashboard window never mounts SessionsView. AppNavigation.swift:64 uses @State selection=.sessions inside NavigationSplitView{List(selection:)} detail:{detailView->SessionsView()} — macOS NavigationSplitView initial programmatic selection commonly does NOT populate the detail pane until a sidebar row is physically clicked, so SessionsView is never instantiated. Also verify the menu-bar popover path (NexusPanel.swift:30 vm.startStreams()) which is the surface Leo most likely clicks. This is the unfinished thread from the dead nx session (it read SessionsView+resolveClients, never AppNavigation). P1: core user journey (dashboard) fully blocked. Relates nx-xzxwr, nx-4ohfs.
close_reason: FIXED + runtime-proven (2026-05-19). Root cause: AppNavigation NavigationSplitView initial programmatic selection never mounted SessionsView -> .task -> startStreams never fired. Fix eb4bd737: shared SessionObserver on always-rendering WindowGroup root + .task on NavigationSplitView. Proof: app self-test 0->1 reachable / 0->58 sessions merged; homelab ss shows 6 ESTABLISHED macbook->homelab conns (was 0); dashboard screenshot shows 5 active sessions rendered.

comments.author: Leonardo Acosta
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed runtime): AppNavigation.swift:64-97 — NavigationSplitView { List(selection: $selection) } detail: { detailView } with @State selection initialized programmatically. On macOS the detail pane does NOT instantiate the selected destination until a sidebar row is physically clicked, so SessionsView() (the ONLY caller of SessionObserver.startStreams() at SessionsView.swift:38) was never created on launch -> .task never ran -> NexusAggregateClient.fetchSessions() NEVER invoked (verified: zero [aggregate] log lines before fix).

FIX (minimal, in-scope): hoisted ONE shared SessionObserver to AppNavigation (the always-rendering WindowGroup root) as @StateObject; start streams via .task on the NavigationSplitView itself; SessionsView now consumes the injected observer (init(observer:)) and only self-manages stop-on-disappear when it owns the lifecycle (ownsLifecycle flag) so tab nav doesn't kill the shared poll/SSE. Files: AppNavigation.swift, SessionsView.swift. Popover path (NexusPanel -> vm.startStreams in .onAppear) was already sound — not touched. resolveClients()/endpoint/agents.toml/NexusAggregateClient untouched.

RUNTIME PROOF: clean before/after, ATS-plist reverted so only the wiring fix is in play. BEFORE opening dashboard window: 0 [aggregate] lines. AFTER cmd-D opens the dashboard window: 8 [aggregate] lines incl. `[aggregate] fetchSessions: agent 'pinned' ...` and the didLogSelfTest line `[aggregate] 1 agents configured, 0 reachable, 0 sessions merged` (NexusAggregateClient.swift:140 — only emits after the full fanOut fetch completes). startStreams()+refreshSessions() now reliably fire on dashboard appear.

SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING ISSUE (NOT nx-t9wrj, NOT client-code): the fetch now fires but fails with ATS NSURLErrorDomain -1022 (cleartext HTTP to http://100.73.182.4:7400 blocked). Isolated test proved this is environmental, not a code bug: a bare swiftc binary with NO bundle -> HTTP 200; ANY .app bundle (even hand-built + ad-hoc-signed WITH NSAllowsArbitraryLoads) -> -1022 on this unsigned-dev machine. Info.plist NSAppTransportSecurity exception is ignored without Developer ID / properly trusted signing. Adding the ATS key to Info.plist did NOT work (tested, reverted). This needs a separate beads issue + user/architectural decision (proper code-signing, or HTTPS on the agent). Filing follow-up.

title: t3-turbo vs t3 dispatch mismatch: T3-Docker projects fall through to default
description:
Audit nx-eg47m (2026-05-18, commit 2d2bd4f) surfaced a silent regression in the existing T3 fleet:

scripts/lib/stack-detect.sh:32-87 emits stack='t3-turbo' (canonical detection)
commands/apply/all.md:611-627 case statement only branches on 't3' (NOT 't3-turbo')

Result: t3-turbo projects (the entire main T3 fleet — oo, tc, tl, mv, ss, etc.) fall through to default in dispatch. T3-Docker variants get nothing. Hot-patch candidate before any larger refactor lands.

Hot-patch options:
1. Add ;; t3-turbo|t3-docker) ... ;; to the case statements (extends existing pattern; ~5 LOC change)
2. Normalize stack-detect.sh to return 't3' and use a sub-profile field for variants (cleaner; larger blast radius)

Recommend Option 1 as the hot-patch; defer Option 2 to the proper registry refactor (nx-d8l1t scaffold).

Affected sites (per audit):
- commands/apply/all.md:611-627 (Phase 3 engineer dispatch)
- commands/apply/references/stacks.md:322-413 (gate dispatch)
- commands/apply/references/stacks.md:280-296 (the aspirational PROFILE_AGENT_MAP)

Source: nx-eg47m audit findings #2.

P1: silently mis-routing across the entire T3 fleet.
notes:
CONFIRMED via direct grep 2026-05-18:
- stack-detect.sh emits: t3-turbo, t3-docker, effect, meta, go-cli, dotnet-next
- case statements in apply/all.md branch on: t3, effect, meta only

Impact scope: every T3 project (the entire main fleet — oo, tc, tl, mv, ss, la, ct, cx, hl, if, tm) silently falls through to default dispatch. T3-Docker variants get no dispatch. go-cli and dotnet-next projects have NO dispatch path at all.

This is why spine-migration v2 needed --stack=meta override repeatedly: t3-turbo wasn't matching the t3 case, so it was treated as unknown, which surfaced as 'phase agents skip / no work happens'.

Hot-patch (P1, ~10 LOC):
- apps/all.md case: add t3-turbo|t3-docker to t3) branch
- references/stacks.md gate case: add t3-turbo|t3-docker to t3) branch
- Optional: add go-cli + dotnet-next placeholder branches that point to general-purpose engineer

Validation:
- Re-run /apply:all on any T3 project with --cost-preview: should detect stack=t3-turbo AND show DB/API/UI/E2E phase agents resolved (not empty)
- Test against an actually-broken case: oo or tc with a spec that has DB+API tasks; verify the right engineer agents get dispatched

title: Author generic verification gates (xcodegen-spec-check, xcodebuild-canary, drizzle-dry-run, shell-deploy-pipefail)
description:
Author 4 verification gates that work on ANY project of the matching kind. Each gate is generic and wired into the swift-bun-hybrid stack profile, NOT bound to Nexus paths.

Gates:
- xcodegen-spec-check — validates project.yml against generated .xcodeproj; runs on any xcodegen-managed Swift project. Takes the project.yml path as arg.
- xcodebuild-canary — smoke-build of a single target/scheme pair to catch compile breaks early. Takes target + scheme args; works on any Xcode project.
- drizzle-dry-run — runs drizzle-kit generate --dry-run to surface schema drift before commit. Takes workspace filter as arg (e.g. --filter @nexus/db OR @oo/db). Works on any Drizzle-managed package.
- shell-deploy-pipefail — static-audits any bash deploy script for missing 'set -euo pipefail', unchecked exit codes, missing trap handlers. Takes a script path; works on any shell deploy.

Wiring:
- Each gate ships as a node script under scripts/bin/gate-* (existing gates pattern)
- Stack profile (nx-aihqs) declares which gates run per phase
- Phase model (nx-r71iw) maps phase → gate set
- Gates exit 0 on pass, non-zero on fail, emit JSON when called with --json (data-producer convention)

Project-agnostic by design: gates accept project.yml path / target name / workspace filter / script path as args. They do NOT hardcode 'NexusShared' or 'nexus-agent'.

Out of scope: T3 gates (eslint, vitest, drizzle migration-on-deploy) untouched. The new gates are additive.
close_reason: 4 gates authored + smoke-tested locally. Generic (project-agnostic); each ships in ~/.claude/scripts/bin/. Smoke results: xcodegen-spec-check=clean, xcodebuild-canary=clean (uses -showBuildSettings since -dry-run removed in modern xcodebuild), drizzle-dry-run=clean (reconstructs migrated state from SQL files; robust to drizzle-kit generate --custom), shell-deploy-pipefail-audit=clean (install.sh hardened today; recognises both 'set -o pipefail' and per-pipe PIPESTATUS recovery). Committed in ce8ef1f0.

title: xcodegen multi-platform NexusShared target silently drops sources
description:
apps/swift/project.yml declares NexusShared with platform: [macOS, iOS, watchOS]. xcodegen 2.45.4 silently emits spec validation errors ('invalid dependency: NexusShared' for 5 consumer targets) and generates a NexusShared target that only includes 2 of 5 source subdirectories (Storage + Synthesis present; Models + Networking + Observers DROPPED).

Verified 2026-05-18 on this Mac:
- Models/Session.swift, Models/HealthSnapshot.swift, Models/Notification.swift, etc. ALL declared 'public' in their source files
- xcodegen omits them from NexusShared.swiftmodule build manifest
- Result: 'error: no type named Session in module NexusShared' at every consumer (nexus-mac Models.swift typealiases, NexusClient.swift, etc.)
- abi.json shows NexusShared.ABIRoot.children = null (empty module)

Workaround verified: switching to 'platform: macOS' restores all 5 subdirs in pbxproj.

Real fix needed: refactor NexusShared into either (a) 3 explicit per-platform targets (NexusShared-macOS, NexusShared-iOS, NexusShared-watchOS) sharing sources via 'sources: - path: NexusShared', OR (b) use xcodegen's 'supportedDestinations' syntax which is the modern multi-platform spec, OR (c) reference NexusShared as 'NexusShared_macOS' from nexus-mac etc.

Pre-existing since wave 3 v2 (add-nexus-shared-framework, commit 8967884 / 2026-05-17). The Nexus.app currently at /Applications/Nexus.app was built BEFORE Models/Networking/Observers subdirs were added, which is why nobody noticed until xcodebuild was actually re-run today.

Priority P1: blocks ALL future Swift builds (xcodebuild fails on every commit touching NexusShared types). xcodegen is the canonical regen tool — current project.pbxproj is a pre-regression cached artifact.

Discovered during nx-455hi verification 2026-05-18.

title: Bug: /events/stream SSE handler closes connection immediately after initial connected event
description:
ROOT CAUSE (verified 2026-04-26):

The /events/stream SSE handler at apps/agent/src/routes/events-sse.ts:93 (handleEventsStream) sends the initial keepalive comment and connected event, then the connection closes within milliseconds. This breaks all downstream consumers including the Mac nexus-notifier daemon.

REPRODUCER (zero-setup):
```bash
curl -sN --no-buffer -v -H "x-nexus-secret: $NEXUS_ATTACH_SECRET" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" http://localhost:7400/events/stream
```

Output:
```
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
: keepalive

data: {"type":"connected","timestamp":"..."}

* transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining
```

EVIDENCE:
- Mac nexus-notifier.sh has logged 15,159 'stream disconnected, reconnecting in 5s' events since 2026-04-24 17:13
- ~16-second cycle: 5s sleep + ~11s connection lifetime
- ~70% of NotificationFired events lost
- Reproducible from localhost (rules out Tailscale/network)
- Reproducible against running binary at ~/.local/bin/nexus-agent (built 2026-04-24 14:03)

UPSTREAM IMPACT:
- TTS notifications from cc/oo/tc/etc. silently lost most of the time
- Architecture comment at apps/agent/src/notifications/channels/tts.ts:18 broken
- 2026-04-26 cc spec migrate-socat-to-nx-notify exposed this — pre-migration the dead UNIX-socket path masked the bug

LIKELY FIX AREAS (apps/agent/src/routes/events-sse.ts):
1. ReadableStream's start() callback may complete synchronously without retaining controller; consider switching to async pull() pattern or explicit controller retention
2. Bun v1.3.11 may have a known SSE/ReadableStream issue with chunked responses — check Bun changelog and known issues
3. Check if any middleware/wrapper between dispatchHandler and the actual response is consuming or closing the stream
4. Verify lifecycleBus.onAny() doesn't throw — if start() throws, controller closes
5. Compare against the WORKING SSE example in spec-events route (apps/agent/src/routes/events-sse.ts also has handleSpecEventsStream which fires 'spec-events SSE client disconnected' — does THAT one work? If yes, diff the two)

CROSS-REF:
- cc-side bead cc-dqmq6 (closed) has full Linux-side verification ladder
- nx-deploy script previously used SSH+nc → now uses nx_notify → POSTs to Linux nexus-agent /notifications/send (works) → fires NotificationFired on lifecycleBus → /events/stream SHOULD push to subscribers (broken)
- Mac listener at /Users/leonardoacosta/bin/nexus-notifier.sh subscribes to /events/stream and pipes 'tts' channel through /usr/bin/say

VERIFICATION (when fix lands):
- Test reproducer above — connection should stay alive past 30s (first keepalive)
- Mac listener disconnect count should drop to ~zero per day (just normal restarts)
- Send 5 nx_notify dispatches in succession; all 5 should produce audio on Mac
close_reason: Fixed in 0195676: set Bun.serve idleTimeout to 255s. Verified end-to-end: Linux agent survives 13s SSE hold, Mac agent survives 13s SSE hold, Mac nexus-notifier zero disconnects in 3+ min (vs 16s cycle before).

title: [project-registry] No tilde expansion on projectsDir — ~ paths silently fail
description: Route handler at projects-discovered.ts:65-107 does not expand ~ or normalize paths. Absolute paths are required but not enforced. A user config with ~/projects as projectsDir will cause readdirSync to silently return empty results. Fix: use path.resolve() with os.homedir() expansion.

title: [project-registry] No FK on sessions.project — orphaned entries accumulate
description: sessions.project field has no foreign key constraint. Projects are purely derived via aggregation — if sessions are deleted, orphaned project entries accumulate indefinitely with no cleanup mechanism. There is no master projects table; the domain relies entirely on session aggregation. Fix: define explicit project lifecycle or add cleanup job.

title: [project-registry] DiscoveredProjectsResponse schema mismatch vs core type
description: Handler at projects-discovered.ts:127-131 returns {projects, projectsDir, total} but the core TypeScript type expects {projects, truncated}. API contract is broken — clients reading the truncated field get undefined. Fix: align handler response shape to match DiscoveredProjectsResponse type definition.

title: [terminal-attach] streamManager.shutdown() never called — PTY processes leak on SIGTERM
description: index.ts shutdown() at lines 46-53 calls server.stop(), sessionManager.stop(), watcherBridge.shutdown(), healthScheduler.stop(), stopRetention() — but NOT streamManager.shutdown(). Active PTY processes and WebSocket viewers are orphaned on SIGTERM/SIGINT. Fix: add streamManager.shutdown() to the shutdown sequence.
close_reason: Original audit bead for streamManager SIGTERM leak — resolved by task 2.10 of finalize-audit-cleanup. streamManager.shutdown() is now invoked inside the SIGTERM handler in apps/agent/src/index.ts before server/DB teardown, bounded by a 5s grace window and wrapped in try/catch.

title: [terminal-attach] No rate limiting — unbounded WebSocket connections exhaust resources
description: allSockets Set and sessions Map in server.ts:43 grow unboundedly. A buggy client or attacker on Tailscale can exhaust memory or file descriptors by opening thousands of WebSocket connections. Fix: add MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS limit with 429 response when exceeded.
close_reason: Verified against current code — MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS = 50 at server-websocket.ts:27; 429 returned on /sessions/:id/stream, /sessions/:id/interact, /ws/federation (lines 164/195/217); test [2.2] at server-websocket-lifecycle.test.ts:20 opens 50 sockets and asserts 51st gets 429. Landed in 2026-04-04-fix-terminal-attach-security.

title: [terminal-attach] No auth on WebSocket PTY attach — any Tailscale peer has shell
description: Any device on the Tailscale network can connect to /sessions/{id}/stream or /sessions/{id}/interact and gain full PTY read/write access. isTailscaleOrigin check only sets CORS response headers — it never blocks non-browser clients. curl/wscat bypass entirely. Fix: require X-Nexus-Secret header validation before WebSocket upgrade.

title: [notification] No timeout on speak_from_socket() — engine can block indefinitely
description: handle_request() at service.rs:104-105 makes TTS API HTTP call with no timeout. If TTS API hangs, the entire notification engine thread blocks indefinitely — no other notifications are delivered. Fix: add .timeout(Duration::from_secs(5)) to the reqwest request.
close_reason: Stale — filed against old Rust notification engine (speak_from_socket). TS rewrite at apps/agent/src/notifications/channels/tts.ts:33 already uses timeout: 5_000 via fetchWithTimeout. Verified: no blocking call possible — all fetch calls wrap AbortController with 5s timeout.

title: [notification] speak_from_socket() returns void — delivery failures silent
description: speak_from_socket() at service.rs:73-112 returns () and swallows HTTP errors. Callers cannot detect delivery failures. No Sentry error event emitted on failure. Fix: change return type to Result<bool>, propagate HTTP errors, emit sentry::capture_event on failure.
close_reason: Stale — filed against old Rust notification engine (speak_from_socket). TS rewrite at apps/agent/src/notifications/channels/tts.ts:40-51 uses logger.error on non-OK response and on catch, so delivery failures are observable via structured logs. Return type is Promise<void> per sendTtsNotification signature (router.ts:5,53); caller doesn't need a return since failures are logged.

title: [tui] unwrap() on reqwest client builder inside tokio::select! panics
description: reqwest::Client::builder().build().unwrap() at main.rs:735 is inside a tokio::select! loop. If build() fails (e.g. TLS init error), the unwrap panics and kills all background polling. Fix: propagate the error via ? or log-and-continue instead of unwrap.

title: [health] Rust MachineHealth / TypeScript HealthMetrics type mismatch
description: Rust uses MachineHealth with f32 GB values; TypeScript HealthMetrics uses detailed per-field CPU/RAM/disk breakdown. Scheduled migration from Rust to TS agent v2 may mask integration gaps. Cross-layer type contract is unverified. Fix: align both to a canonical schema in nexus-core/types/health.ts + generate Rust types from it.

title: [session-mgmt] VALID_STATUSES filter missing 'stale' and 'errored'
description: GET /sessions VALID_STATUSES array at routes/sessions.ts:10 is missing 'stale' and 'errored' values. TypeScript Session type declares these as valid SessionStatus values, but the route returns 400 Bad Request if any caller tries to filter for them. Fix: add both to VALID_STATUSES.

title: [session-mgmt] No duplicate session guard in register_managed
description: handle_start_session called twice with same project registers two sessions with distinct UUIDs and spawns two concurrent bootstrap claude processes. register_adhoc uses Entry API (preventing duplicates) but register_managed has no such guard. Fix: add idempotency check on project path before registration.

title: [session-mgmt] Spawn failure leaks orphaned session in registry
description: handle_start_session does NOT clean up the already-registered session when bootstrap spawn fails — session leaks as Warming/orphaned with no valid PID or process. Fix: wrap registration+spawn in a transaction pattern; rollback registry entry on spawn Err.

title: [credential-mgmt] Security hardening — token exposure + plaintext storage
description: Audit wave findings for credential-mgmt domain. Key issues: CredentialAccount derives Serialize without #[serde(skip)] on access_token, value_encrypted field stores plaintext (misleading name), non-constant-time secret comparison, TOCTOU race in lease(). 11 total findings.

title: [project-registry] API schema + data integrity fixes
description: Audit wave findings for project-registry domain. Key issues: DiscoveredProjectsResponse schema mismatch ({projects,projectsDir,total} vs expected {projects,truncated}), no FK on sessions.project, no tilde expansion on projectsDir path. 25 total findings spanning API, data, and UI layers.

title: [session-management] Session lifecycle correctness
description: Audit wave findings for session-management domain. Key issues: spawn failure leaks registered session (orphaned session in registry), no duplicate session guard allows double-registration, VALID_STATUSES filter missing 'stale'/'errored' values causing 400 errors, all integration tests skipped post-PG migration.

title: [terminal-attach] Security + Reliability hardening
description: Audit wave findings for terminal-attach domain. Key issues: no auth on WebSocket PTY attach (any Tailscale peer has full shell access), no rate limiting on connections, streamManager.shutdown() never called on SIGTERM causing PTY leaks. Priority: P1 security and reliability fixes before any external usage.

title: spec-watcher only polls REGISTERED projects; agent hosts have empty project registry -> /specs always [] despite openspec dirs present
description: ROOT CAUSE (runtime-confirmed homelab 2026-05-19): apps/agent/src/index.ts:166 — startSpecWatcher 'polls openspec status across registered projects'. title: XCUITest cannot deterministically open the LSUIElement dashboard window (blocks integration-gate Tier B 2.2/2.3/2.4)

comments.author: Leonardo Acosta
comments.text:
Blocks add-fullstack-integration-test-gate tasks 2.2 (nx-u17ua), 2.3 (nx-ri6go), 2.4 (nx-9kuwm). Task 2.1 (nx-3ltm0) is DONE and unaffected.

PROBLEM: nexus-mac is `LSUIElement` (menu-bar only, no Dock window). The dashboard is a SwiftUI `WindowGroup(id:"dashboard")` opened in production only via the popover's Cmd+D. XCUITest needs that window to appear to assert section rendering / transport. Investigated mechanisms, with runtime evidence:

1. `.background(View).onAppear` hook on the MenuBarExtra label → NEVER fires (MenuBarExtra label view lifecycle does not run at launch). 0/3 window appears.
2. `.defaultLaunchBehavior(.presented)` on the WindowGroup (macOS 15+, via @SceneBuilder + availability-gated Scene extension — `else` is forbidden in SceneBuilder, confirmed via Apple docs) → NON-DETERMINISTIC under the XCUITest harness: observed 0/3 and 1/3 window-appears across identical runs. Root cause: `.presented` only fires "in the absence of previously RESTORED scenes" (Apple docs); XCUITest's repeated launch/terminate leaves scene-restoration state, so 2nd/3rd test in a run sees a restored scene and does not present. Disabling state persistence (`-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState YES`) made it 0/3 (removed even the lucky restoration).

EVIDENCE THE REST OF THE HARNESS IS CORRECT (so this is purely the window-open seam):
- `testMenuBarSurfaceAndCommandsReachable` (2.3) PASSED twice (run8 8.77s, run9 12.58s) — proves scheme wiring, the nexus-mac-Tests TEST_HOST fix, ad-hoc signing (app+runner+xctest), runner attach, and the test logic all work; only the window mechanism is flaky.
- stub-agent CLI (`bun stub-agent.ts`) binds NON-loopback (10.61.142.78), prints STUB_BASE_URL, serves the fixture; loopback guard throws on 127.0.0.1 (enforced spec scenario verified). The 2.4 transport substrate is proven; only the dashboard render assertion is gated by the window seam.
- XCUITest runner attaches only after ad-hoc signing app+runner+xctest (CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO alone → "Test crashed with signal kill before establishing connection"). nexus-mac has sandbox/aps/icloud entitlements requiring a dev cert this env lacks; ad-hoc sign post-build is the workaround.

DEFERRED SCOPE DECISION (needs user/architecture call — Breaking Changes Policy):
- A genuinely deterministic seam is an NSApplicationDelegateAdaptor opening the window in applicationDidFinishLaunching, but bridging AppKit→SwiftUI `openWindow(id:)` on the macOS 14 deployment target has no clean supported path.
- Converting the dashboard `WindowGroup`→`Window` (singleton) makes `.defaultLaunchBehavior(.presented)` deterministic (Apple's documented example uses `Window`), but changes production window semantics (multi vs single) — a behavior change I did NOT make unilaterally.
- Recommended: either (a) accept a `Window` (singleton) dashboard if multi-window isn't required, or (b) add a small AppKit launch path. Either is a design decision for the spec owner.

Stale-fixture sub-issue: a successful 2.4 round-trip would still paint an empty dashboard because SESSIONS_FIXTURE's FIXED_NOW timestamp is filtered by SessionObserver.activeSessions' 300s freshness window. A serve-time freshener was prototyped but it breaks the API-batch's stub-agent.test.ts (which deep-equals the snapshot). A future 2.4 implementation needs a non-snapshot-breaking freshen path (e.g. opt-in `?fresh=1` query param or a startStubAgent option) — design decision deferred here.

All 2.2/2.3/2.4-only scaffolding (IntegrationGateUITests.swift, accessibility identifiers in AppNavigation/SessionsView, the nexusApp launch seam, the stub freshener+CLI) was REVERTED to keep the repo clean (no shipped untested/flaky code). The reusable infra that IS correct and stays: project.yml scheme.testTargets wiring + nexus-mac-Tests TEST_HOST fix + the regenerated shared scheme.

comments.author: Leonardo Acosta
comments.text:
RESOLVED. Both authorized decisions implemented; all 3 XCUITests pass deterministically (3 consecutive full runs, 0 failures each).

1. WindowGroup → singleton Window (user-authorized breaking change): dashboard scene in nexusApp.swift is now `Window("Nexus Dashboard", id:"dashboard")` + `.defaultLaunchBehavior(.presented)` via an availability-gated Scene extension. This made `.presented` restoration-independent — the flakiness (was 0/3–1/3 window-appears) is gone (now 3/3 across 3 runs). Single-dashboard-window production semantics accepted.

2. Test-only entitlements strip: new apps/swift/nexus/nexus/nexus-uitest.entitlements (only network.client; drops app-sandbox/aps/icloud which need a dev cert). Wired ONLY via the xcodebuild test CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS override (production/release keep nexus.entitlements). With this + ad-hoc sign (CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- / CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=YES) the unsigned XCUITest runner attaches (was: "crashed with signal kill before establishing connection"). Test targets also got GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE: YES so they're signable.

Residual sub-issue SOLVED (2.4): the sandboxed nexus-mac-UITests-Runner (network.client only, no network.server) cannot let a test-spawned stub bind ANY listening socket (EADDRINUSE, loopback or not). The non-loopback bind is load-bearing (loopback is ATS-exempt → false-green). Resolution: deploy/run-tier-b-xcuitests.sh starts the stub OUTSIDE the sandbox (non-loopback), exports TEST_RUNNER_NX_STUB_BASE_URL (xcodebuild's documented channel — forwarded into the runner as NX_STUB_BASE_URL with prefix stripped). StubAgentProcess.start() prefers the harness URL (sandbox-safe), self-spawn only as a non-sandboxed fallback. The app still does the real cleartext round-trip so ATS -1022 is faithfully guarded.

Stale-fixture sub-issue SOLVED without breaking the API batch: stub-agent.ts serves fresh startedAt/lastActivity ONLY for `/sessions?withFingerprint=true` (the real client path). Plain `/sessions` (no query) stays the exact SESSIONS_FIXTURE snapshot, so the API-batch stub-agent.test.ts deep-equal stays green (verified: 9 pass, 0 fail).

RUNTIME EVIDENCE (deploy/run-tier-b-xcuitests.sh):
- "Tier B: stub up at http://10.61.142.78:63611" (non-loopback)
- testClientTransportRoundTripAgainstNonLoopbackStub PASSED (11.09s)
- testEveryDashboardSectionRenders PASSED (32.86s)
- testMenuBarSurfaceAndCommandsReachable PASSED (9.22s)
- "Executed 3 tests, with 0 failures" / ** TEST EXECUTE SUCCEEDED **
- 2 additional consecutive re-runs: both "Executed 3 tests, with 0 failures" (deterministic)
- Screenshot /tmp/nx-cap/uibatch-dashboard.png: singleton dashboard, Sessions selected, "1 live" green, the stub fixture row rendered (claude / active / stub-machine = SESSIONS_FIXTURE[0]) — proves real cleartext round-trip with NO ATS -1022.
- No regressions: task 2.1 NexusSharedTests 7/7 pass; API-batch stub test 9/9 pass.

The pre-push gate's existing Tier B hook (deploy/hooks.d/pre-push/01-deploy:126) already calls $DEPLOY_DIR/run-tier-b-xcuitests.sh — now provided, making the gate's "MUST abort the push on Tier B failure" satisfiable.

title: install.sh macOS: find -name 'Nexus.app' misses xcodebuild product 'nexus.app' -> app never installed
description: install.sh:170 — install_macos() does: APP_PATH=$(find $BUILD_DIR -name 'Nexus.app' -type d ...). But scheme nexus-mac / project nexus.xcodeproj produces 'nexus.app' (lowercase). title: macOS deploy hooks sed a deleted plist template -> macbook agent never auto-deploys
description:
WHY: Discovered 2026-05-18 during the homelab post-merge remote-fanout to macbook (deploying nx-z66n8). Error: 'sed: /Users/leonardoacosta/dev/nx/deploy/com.nexus.agent.plist: No such file or directory'.

ROOT CAUSE: deploy/install.sh:191-194 migrated agent plist install to INLINE generation (heredoc embedding env, avoids $USER/$HOME drift) and DELETED the checked-in template deploy/com.nexus.agent.plist. But both git deploy hooks were never updated and still reference the deleted template:
  - deploy/hooks.d/post-merge/02-deploy:156  sed "s|${USER}|$USER|g" "$DEPLOY_DIR/com.nexus.agent.plist" > "$PLIST"
  - deploy/hooks.d/pre-push/01-deploy:112    (identical line)
$DEPLOY_DIR=$REPO_DIR/deploy, so the path resolves to the removed file. sed fails BUT the '> $PLIST' redirect still creates an EMPTY ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.nexus.agent.plist, which bootstrap_with_retry then tries to load -> launchd gets garbage.

IMPACT: macOS Darwin branch only. Every (a) macbook git pull/post-merge, (b) any push triggering pre-push on macOS, (c) homelab->macbook remote fanout silently fails to deploy/start the macbook nexus-agent. Consistent with observed state: no nexus-agent process/socket on macbook this session. NOT production-down (dashboard reads homelab; manual deploy/install.sh still works via inline gen) -> P2 not P1. Masks future macbook-agent work and spams every fanout.

WHAT: make the hooks generate the plist the same way install.sh does, instead of sed-ing a file that no longer exists.
design:
OPTIONS:
A. Hooks delegate to deploy/install.sh — REJECTED: install.sh has no agent-only flag; it unconditionally runs xcodegen+xcodebuild (full Swift dashboard build) on Darwin. Would drag an Xcode build into every push.
B. (RECOMMENDED) Extract install.sh's inline plist heredoc into a shared sourced helper (new deploy/lib/gen-agent-plist.sh exposing gen_agent_plist <dest>); source+call from install.sh AND both hooks. Kills the duplication/drift class that caused this bug (single source of truth for plist content). No deploy/lib/ exists yet — create it.
C. Restore checked-in deploy/com.nexus.agent.plist — REJECTED: reintroduces the exact $USER/$HOME drift install.sh:191-194 deleted it to fix.
QUICK-FIX FALLBACK (if Leo wants minimal patch first): replace the broken sed line in both hooks with the same inline heredoc install.sh uses (3 copies, unblocks deploy, but re-creates drift risk — only as a stopgap before B).

VERIFY: after fix, on macbook run the pre-push hook path (or SKIP_DEPLOY=0 git push) and homelab->macbook fanout; assert ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.nexus.agent.plist is non-empty + valid (plutil -lint) and launchctl list shows com.nexus.agent with a live PID.
notes: Fix scoped + scaffolded as OpenSpec proposal remove-macos-deploy-agent-daemon (feature nx-pvc4n, epic nx-1hluw [CAPABILITY] systemd-service). Decision: Option D (remove Mac daemon path) — Option B superseded after discovery found remove-mac-deploy-artifacts + env-aware-install-script mandate no macOS agent daemon. Close this bug when nx-pvc4n ships.
close_reason: Fixed + runtime-verified via remove-macos-deploy-agent-daemon (commit 23ba08f). Dead macOS daemon path removed from both deploy hooks + install.sh inline plist-gen; drift guard added (deploy/check-no-mac-daemon.sh). title: Swift dashboard: multi-agent aggregation via agents.toml (peer-connector replacement)
description:
The Swift dashboard (nx-gaquu, 10 views) only queries a single hardcoded NexusEndpoint.localhost (localhost:7400). Per .claude/CLAUDE.md § Topology, Swift clients SHOULD 'discover agents via ~/.config/nexus/agents.toml and aggregate sessions over the network.' That aggregation layer was never built.

History: spine-migration v2's remove-peer-connector (commit d2e965e, 2026-05-17) deleted the agent-side WebSocket federation (homelab pushed events to Mac via /ws/federation). The intended replacement was Swift-side pull aggregation: each client reads agents.toml, queries every agent's /sessions + /health + SSE streams, merges results. remove-peer-connector shipped the deletion; the Swift replacement was scoped but never implemented.

Symptom that surfaced this (2026-05-18): user opened the dashboard, all views empty. Root cause chain (first 3 fixed today):
1. DB migrations never applied to shared homelab postgres (FIXED — 31 migrations applied)
2. pgrep blocked by safe-spawn allowlist, no reconciliation (FIXED — commit 48f3b72)
3. homelab agent ran stale pre-spine-migration binary (FIXED — redeployed via post-merge hook)
4. THIS ISSUE: even healthy, the Mac dashboard hits localhost:7400 (Mac agent, currently down + in launchctl I/O wedge) — never sees homelab's 19 live sessions

Scope:
- NexusShared: add AgentRegistry that parses ~/.config/nexus/agents.toml ([[agents]] name/host/port/user)
- NexusClient: accept multiple endpoints OR add a NexusAggregateClient that fans out
- SessionObserver + the 10 dashboard view-models: consume the aggregate, tag each row with its source agent (the 'machine'/'originAgent' field already exists in the Session model)
- SettingsStore: optional 'primary endpoint' override + per-agent enable/disable
- Handle partial failures gracefully (one agent down != whole dashboard empty)

Quick-override interim shipped same-day (separate small commit): SettingsStore endpoint override so dashboard can point directly at homelab while this lands.

Parent: nx-ma6h8 (spine-migration). Priority P2 (dashboards are non-functional for the multi-machine case without it).
close_reason: Multi-agent agents.toml aggregation shipped. AgentRegistry + NexusAggregateClient + SessionObserver rewire + 8 direct-client view-models. Partial-failure tolerant (homelab-up/Mac-down verified: 2 agents configured, 1 reachable, 6 sessions merged, dashboard non-empty). Interim single-endpoint override folded in as a pin escape-hatch + cleared on this Mac. NexusClient unchanged. Build clean (BUILD SUCCEEDED), menubar bounced (pid 49053), runtime-proven. Last architectural gap from spine-migration v2 closed.

title: fix(swift): SessionsView SessionObserver default init crosses main-actor boundary
description:
SessionsView.swift line 18:

  public init(observer: SessionObserver = SessionObserver()) {

Compile error during nexus-mac build (xcodebuild 2026-05-18):

  error: call to main actor-isolated initializer 'init(client:notificationCap:)' in a synchronous nonisolated context

NexusShared.SessionObserver.init is @MainActor-isolated:
  @MainActor public init(client: NexusShared.NexusClient = NexusClient(), notificationCap: Int = 50)

But SessionsView.init is a synchronous nonisolated context, so the default argument expression
SessionObserver() can't be evaluated.

Likely fix: either mark SessionsView.init as @MainActor, or remove the default argument and
construct SessionObserver inside an .onAppear / .task / via @StateObject(wrappedValue:) where
MainActor is available.

Surfaced after fixing the NexusClient type-shadowing bug (the build couldn't reach this point
before). Unrelated error class — separate task.
close_reason: Fixed all three classes targeted by this issue: (1) SessionsView MainActor via @MainActor on struct + dual-init pattern (default-arg evaluation can't cross actor boundary even with @MainActor on init alone — needed two overloads), (2) swept CcProfile shadowing in CredentialsView via NexusShared.CcProfile qualifier (legacy nexus/nexus/CcProfileStatusView.swift has incompatible shape), (3) added import NexusShared to ElevenLabsSettingsView for Keychain/KeychainAccount/ElevenLabsClient. Build still fails on UNRELATED PtyViewer SwiftTerm errors (Color ambiguity + TerminalViewDelegate conformance) — split out as nx-m40q7 per Scope Explosion rule. nx-3pka7 scope complete; Nexus.app rebuild/install/bounce deferred to after nx-m40q7.

title: install.sh: launchd plist missing NEXUS_ENCRYPTION_KEY env var
description:
deploy/install.sh § 'Agent launchd plist' generates ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.nexus.agent.plist without sourcing NEXUS_ENCRYPTION_KEY (or NEXUS_ATTACH_SECRET, POSTGRES_URL) from ~/.config/nexus/secrets.env.

Result: agent fails fast on startup with 'Encryption key validation failed — agent cannot start' and KeepAlive thrashes (943 restarts observed before fix).

Manual repair applied during nx-0t3n0:
- Generated NEXUS_ENCRYPTION_KEY via openssl rand -hex 32 (already existed in secrets.env)
- Wrote new plist with EnvironmentVariables block containing the three keys
- launchctl bootout + bootstrap; agent now running at pid 51498 with /health responding

Fix proposal: install.sh should:
1. Source secrets.env if it exists
2. Generate NEXUS_ENCRYPTION_KEY if missing, persist to secrets.env
3. Emit those env vars into the plist EnvironmentVariables block

Surfaced during nx-0t3n0.
close_reason: Fixed in deploy/install.sh 2026-05-18 (this commit). Script now sources ~/.config/nexus/secrets.env before generating plist, then iterates known keys (NEXUS_ENCRYPTION_KEY, NEXUS_ATTACH_SECRET, POSTGRES_URL, APNS_*, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY) and embeds non-empty values into the EnvironmentVariables block with proper XML escaping. Smoke-tested: re-ran install.sh --no-build, generated plist contains all 5 NEXUS_*/APNS_* vars correctly. Agent boots cleanly from launchd without manual env hand-rolling.

title: DECISION: refactor existing stack-toolchain vs extend in-place vs ship as new skill
description:
Architectural decision for integrating siblings nx-aihqs (stack profile), nx-r71iw (phase model), nx-ppy42 (engineer agents), nx-xkz22 (verification gates), nx-pzexe (skills) into /apply + /apply:all.

DEPENDS ON: nx-eg47m (AUDIT) — do not start until audit closes.

Three viable approaches:

(1) EXTEND IN-PLACE — add new profile rows to stacks.md, append phase entries to phases.md, drop new skills/agents into existing tree.
  + Additive, low blast radius, no breaking changes to T3 flow
  - May bloat stacks.md / phases.md over time
  - Couples toolchain extensibility to single file growth

(2) REFACTOR INTO 'stack-profiles' SKILL — extract stack-handling into a dedicated skill loaded by /apply, with profile entries as data (yaml or json registry).
  + Cleaner separation, easier to extend (just register a new profile entry)
  + Discoverability via skill catalog
  - Higher initial refactor cost
  - Refactor risk to T3 fleet (must preserve t3-turbo + meta behavior exactly)

(3) STANDALONE OPT-IN SKILL — ship swift-bun-hybrid pieces as a self-contained skill that consuming projects opt into via CLAUDE.md import.
  + Zero risk to existing toolchain
  + Project chooses opt-in explicitly
  - Discoverability worse (skill must be named by project)
  - Code duplication if multiple hybrid stacks emerge

Decision criteria (weight per audit findings):
- Maintainability: how does this scale to 3rd/4th non-T3 stack profile?
- Fleet impact: T3 projects MUST keep working unchanged
- Discoverability: how does a future project find this profile?
- Refactor blast radius: lines touched in /apply.md + /apply:all.md
- Reversibility: if approach fails, can it be undone cleanly?

Output: a decision record (markdown) attached as a bd note, naming the chosen approach + rationale. The implementation child (nx-xxxxx — see linked) gets shaped from this decision.

NO IMPLEMENTATION until this decision lands.

title: Author bun-patterns + swift-framework-patterns + shell-deploy-patterns skills (generic)
description:
Author 3 generic skills consumed by the swift-bun-hybrid stack profile. Skill names DROP the 'nexus-' prefix — they describe patterns for the technology, not for Nexus specifically.

Skills:
- swift-framework-patterns — any multi-platform Swift framework. Covers: Codable bridging between Swift and TS payloads, supportedDestinations syntax in project.yml, Keychain wrapping, AVAudioPlayer patterns, framework-vs-app target split, NotificationCenter observer lifecycle.
- bun-patterns — any Bun service. Covers: socket-server vs http-server choice, mock.module isolation (avoiding test pollution), pino logging with OpenTelemetry, fire-and-forget async patterns, Bun-native API preference over Node compat.
- shell-deploy-patterns — any shell-based deploy (install.sh / launchd / systemd). Covers: set -euo pipefail discipline, trap handlers, idempotent install scripts, env-aware OS detection (Linux systemd vs macOS launchd), Tailscale-bound port discipline.

Skill loaders: stack profile (nx-aihqs) declares which skills load per engineer agent (nx-ppy42).

Project-specific knowledge that stays OUT of these skills:
- NexusShared module structure → ~/dev/nx/.claude/CLAUDE.md
- Nexus-specific socket path (~/.config/nexus/agent.sock) → ~/dev/nx/.claude/CLAUDE.md
- Nexus binary names → ~/dev/nx/.claude/CLAUDE.md
- Per-project env var keys → each project's CLAUDE.md

The skill files document patterns; the CLAUDE.md documents the project's instantiation of those patterns.

Out of scope: existing T3 skills (t3-code-patterns, t3-testing-patterns) untouched.

title: Author swift-engineer + bun-engineer + deploy-engineer agents (generic)
description:
Author 3 engineer agents that handle Swift / Bun / shell-deploy work for ANY project matching the swift-bun-hybrid profile. Agents are project-agnostic — they take direction from the consuming project's CLAUDE.md.

Agents:
- swift-engineer — Swift framework + Apps phase work (xcodegen project.yml edits, Swift source, Codable bridging, supportedDestinations syntax)
- bun-engineer — Bun service phase work (socket servers, hook ingest, pino logging, Bun-native APIs)
- deploy-engineer — Deploy phase work (install.sh, launchd plists, systemd units, shell pipefail discipline)

Skill loading: agents load DOMAIN skills, not project skills:
- swift-engineer loads: swift-framework-patterns (generic), state-handling, verification-before-completion
- bun-engineer loads: bun-patterns (generic), test-driven-development, verification-before-completion
- deploy-engineer loads: shell-deploy-patterns (generic), deploy-and-env, verification-before-completion

Worktree contract: standard pattern from scripts/lib/engineer-preamble.sh emit_engineer_preamble — targeted git add, no git stash, per-worktree isolation. Same contract as t3 engineers.

Frontmatter: each agent declares allowed-tools and the phases it handles in the stack profile.

Project-specific details that DO NOT belong in these agents:
- Module names (NexusShared vs SomeOtherFramework) — comes from project CLAUDE.md
- Env var keys (NEXUS_ENCRYPTION_KEY vs PROJECT_KEY) — comes from project CLAUDE.md
- Binary names (nexus-agent vs other-daemon) — comes from project CLAUDE.md
- Port assignments — comes from project CLAUDE.md

Out of scope: T3 engineer agents (api-engineer, db-engineer, ui-engineer) untouched.

title: Define DB → Service → Framework → Apps → Deploy → E2E phase model (generic)
description:
Define a PHASE MODEL for the swift-bun-hybrid stack profile. Phases are stack-conceptual (not project-specific): each phase name describes a layer of the stack, not a Nexus module name.

Phase order: DB → Service → Framework → Apps → Deploy → E2E

Path-pattern classification (NOT module-name matching):
- packages/db/** → DB
- apps/agent/** OR apps/*-emit/** OR apps/*-service/** → Service
- apps/*/<Framework>/Sources/** OR apps/swift/<Framework>/** → Framework
- apps/swift/<App>/** OR apps/*/Sources/App/** → Apps
- deploy/** OR scripts/install*.sh OR launchd/systemd unit files → Deploy
- e2e/** OR tests/e2e/** → E2E

Framework phase = any multi-platform Swift framework consumed by Apps (NOT 'NexusShared' specifically). Apps phase = the platform-specific Swift apps that depend on Framework.

Refactor-heavy waves: phase classifier MUST return a phase for deletions/moves, not null. Unmapped paths fall through to a default phase (Service or Apps based on path prefix) rather than failing silently — root-cause fix for the spine-migration v2 no-commit-produced bug.

Wiring:
- Phase map encoded in commands/apply/references/phases.md under the swift-bun-hybrid section
- Phase classifier in scripts/bin/wave-plan-build consumes the path patterns
- Engineer agent dispatch keyed on phase name (see nx-ppy42)
- Gate dispatch keyed on phase name (see nx-xkz22)

Out of scope: T3 phase model untouched. Any project not matching swift-bun-hybrid keeps its existing phase model.

title: Define swift-bun-hybrid stack profile (generic)
description:

Detection signals are CHARACTERISTICS, not project names:
- apps/*/project.yml (xcodegen-managed Swift project)
- apps/*/Sources/** OR apps/*/<Framework>/Sources/** (Swift framework)
- apps/agent/package.json with bun runtime declaration (or any apps/* bun service)
- packages/db/drizzle/ (Drizzle-managed migrations)
- ./deploy/install.sh OR shell-based deploy entrypoint

Profile name candidates: swift-bun-hybrid | swiftbun | bsh (pick during implementation; reflect in stacks.md).

Wiring:
- Stack-profile entry in commands/apply/references/stacks.md
- Phase map reference (see nx-r71iw)
- Engineer agent set reference (see nx-ppy42)
- Gate set reference (see nx-xkz22)
- Skill loader reference (see nx-pzexe)

Detection happens via signal-match at /apply:all phase1-bootstrap — NOT via a Nexus-specific path check. Any project matching the signals gets the profile automatically.

Out of scope: project-specific overlays (NexusShared module name, specific env var keys) — those live in each consuming project's .claude/CLAUDE.md.

title: [CAPABILITY] stack-toolchain-extensibility — generalize agent/phase/gate stack beyond T3 fleet

title: Extract processHookEvent helper for socket-dispatcher parity
description:
socket-dispatcher-parity spec demands byte-identical session_events rows + identical lifecycle envelope sequences between HTTP POST /hooks and the AF_UNIX socket dispatcher. Gap audit shows 9 missing concerns on the socket path:

1. Schema-drift detection (inspectAndEmitDrift)
2. session_events persistence (appendSessionEvent)
3. Git project resolver on session_start (resolveGitOrigin)
4. Cost computation on session_summary (computeCostUsd)
5. Hook event throttle (hookEventThrottle.enqueue)
6. lifecycleBus.emit('HookEventReceived') broadcast
7. evaluateAndDispatch notification trigger
8. handleAgentSpawn parent/role enrichment
9. handleStopFailure status=errored

Achieving parity requires extracting routes/hooks.ts handleHooks() body into a shared services/process-hook-event.ts that both routes/hooks.ts and services/socket-server/dispatcher.ts invoke. This is a ~150-line refactor with a 27-event parity test. The HTTP path also currently does credential-fingerprint binding via session_start payload? No — that's socket-only today, so parity also requires HTTP to gain credential binding OR socket to keep it as an enrichment after the shared helper.

Deferring from wave-3 batch — needs its own design pass + runtime verification (parity test must run, not just compile). Recommend treating this as a separate spec or sub-feature.

title: [PROPOSAL] add-hooks-sse-fanout
description:
Re-emit persisted hook events to /events/stream so the Next.js dashboard updates live without polling.

Today, /events/stream broadcasts lifecycleBus events (NotificationFired, SessionStarted, SettingsChanged-future). Hook events that landed in session_events are NOT broadcast, so dashboards must poll /sessions or /failures to see new activity.

Scope:
- After session_events insert in handleHooks, emit a lifecycleBus event (e.g. HookEventReceived with {event_type, session_id, project, event_id}).
- SSE subscribers (apps/nextjs dashboard pages) filter by event_type to refresh their views.
- /session/[id] page uses the stream to live-append a session timeline.
- /projects/[name] uses it to update session-count badges.
- Optional throttle: high-frequency events (tool_use_end on tight loops) batched at 500ms intervals.

Depends on: extend-hooks-event-taxonomy (broadcasting events that don't exist yet is hollow).
Sibling: add-hooks-notification-triggers (independent — both react to recognized events).
Predecessor: restore-hooks-event-persistence (archived 2026-04-27).
close_reason: Proposal applied + archived in apply-2026-04-27-001 hooks-arc plan

title: [PROPOSAL] add-hooks-notification-triggers
description:
Wire selected hook events into the notification pipeline so high-signal CC events surface as desktop/TTS/Slack notifications.

Trigger events (per CC's curated routing policy in telemetry.sh):
- tool_use_fail → desktop + (optionally) Slack
- permission_request → desktop + TTS (interactive — user wants prompt audibility)
- hook_failure → desktop + Slack
- session_stop with crash flag → desktop + Slack
- session_summary on long sessions (cost > threshold) → optional digest

Routing should reuse the existing notification-router rule engine (apps/agent/src/notifications/router.ts). Each event type maps to a small declarative rule with channel set + suppression heuristics (dedupe by tool_name within N seconds, etc.).

Scope:
- Map of event_type → notification template + channels (project-prefixed body).
- Dedupe / coalesce strategy for noisy events (tool_use_fail in tight retry loops).
- Respect notification_settings (when add-notification-control-dashboard ships).
- Tests for each rule firing exactly once per qualifying event.

Depends on: extend-hooks-event-taxonomy (events must be recognized + parsed before they can trigger notifications).
Sibling: add-hooks-sse-fanout (dashboard tail).
Predecessor: restore-hooks-event-persistence (archived 2026-04-27).
close_reason: Proposal applied + archived in apply-2026-04-27-001 hooks-arc plan

title: [PROPOSAL] extend-hooks-event-taxonomy
description:
Extend handleHooks to recognize and persist the ~13 event types CC sends that nexus currently drops into the 'unknown' branch.

Currently handled (post restore-hooks-event-persistence, archived 2026-04-27): session_start, session_stop, stop_success, stop_failure, session_summary, session_heartbeat, diagnostic_ping.

Currently UNHANDLED (drop to default unknown branch — events still 200 but no row written):
  Lifecycle: session_terminate, post_compact, pre_compact
  Agents: agent_spawn, agent_telemetry, agent_complete
  Tools: tool_use_end, tool_use_fail
  Commands: command_start, command_end, user_prompt
  Other: permission_request, teammate_idle, task_completed, instructions_loaded, config_change, worktree_create, worktree_remove, notification, hook_failure

Source of truth for event vocabulary: ~/.claude/scripts/hooks/telemetry.sh (search 'json_event').

Scope:
- Extend HookEventPayload type with the additional fields each event carries (e.g. tool_use_fail brings tool_name, error_message, exit_code).
- Route each event type to a handler that writes to session_events with the right metadata shape. Most need no schema change — session_events.metadata stores the JSON payload.
- A handful (agent_spawn, agent_complete) may benefit from a dedicated table; design decision deferred to /feature spec.

Predecessor: restore-hooks-event-persistence (archived 2026-04-27, commit 436fb37).
Sibling features: extend-hooks-notification-triggers, add-hooks-sse-fanout.
close_reason: Proposal applied + archived in apply-2026-04-27-001 hooks-arc plan

title: Mac nexus-notifier TTS playback overlaps when notifications burst
description:
OBSERVED: When two or more notifications fire within a few seconds, the Mac nexus-notifier launches concurrent backgrounded `say` processes that play simultaneously.

ROOT CAUSE: ~/bin/nexus-notifier.sh _dispatch_tts runs `/usr/bin/say -- "$body" &` — trailing & detaches each say as independent process. No serialization.

PRIOR ART: Nova (~/dev/nv/packages/daemon/src/features/tts/) has a serial queue: single worker owns audio output, requests append to FIFO, worker drains serially.

FIX OPTIONS for nexus-notifier.sh:
  (A) flock-based mutex around `say` — simplest, blocks SSE loop while playing
  (B) Named-pipe queue + drain worker — preferred, non-blocking dispatch with serial playback
  (C) Dedicated launchctl playback service — over-engineered

REPRO: for i in 1 2 3; do nx_notify "Burst test $i"; done — three voices overlap.

ACCEPTANCE:
  - 5 burst nx_notify calls produce 5 sequential utterances
  - SSE listener does not drop events while audio plays
  - Recommend Shape B

title: Mac nexus-notifier TTS playback overlaps when notifications burst
description:
OBSERVED: When two or more notifications fire within a few seconds (common during multi-agent batch operations), the Mac nexus-notifier launches concurrent backgrounded `say` processes that play simultaneously and step on each other.

ROOT CAUSE (verified): In ~/bin/nexus-notifier.sh the _dispatch_tts handler does:

  /usr/bin/say -- "$body" 2>>"$LOG_FILE" &

The trailing & detaches each say invocation as an independent process. There is no serialization, queue, or wait-for-previous mechanism. So a burst of N notifications spawns N concurrent say processes.

PRIOR ART: Nova (~/dev/nv/packages/daemon/src/features/tts/) implements a serial playback queue. Pattern to borrow:
  1. A single playback worker process owns the audio output
  2. Incoming TTS requests append to a queue (file, FIFO, or in-memory)
  3. Worker drains the queue serially: play current item, wait for completion, dequeue next

LIGHTWEIGHT FIX OPTIONS for nexus-notifier.sh (single bash script):
  (A) flock-based mutex around `say` — guarantees no overlap, simplest, blocks the SSE-read loop while playing (a few seconds per notification)
  (B) Named-pipe queue: spawn a single drain worker on script start that reads lines from a FIFO and runs `say` synchronously. Producer (the dispatch handler) just echoes to the FIFO.
  (C) launchctl-managed dedicated playback service that subscribes to a separate event topic — over-engineered for our use case

REPRODUCER:
  source ~/.claude/scripts/lib/nx-send.sh
  for i in 1 2 3; do nx_notify "Burst test message number $i, listen for overlap"; done

EXPECTED: Three sequential utterances played one after another.
ACTUAL: Three voices speaking over each other.

ACCEPTANCE:
  - Burst of 5 nx_notify calls produces 5 sequential, non-overlapping utterances
  - Listener does not lose SSE events while playing (so dispatch must be non-blocking even if playback is serial)
  - Recommendation B (named-pipe + drain worker) preferred for the non-blocking dispatch property

REFERENCE:
  - Nova prior art: ~/dev/nv/packages/daemon/src/features/tts/
  - Affected file: ~/bin/nexus-notifier.sh + nx/deploy/nexus-notifier.sh (after this fix lands)

title: Extend /hooks handler to persist events into dashboards
description:
Context: CC hooks now successfully deliver events to nexus via http://localhost:7400/hooks (migration landed 2026-04-24 from stale unix socket path). The /hooks HTTP handler at apps/agent/src/routes/hooks.ts currently only logs events via pino and returns 200 ack — it does not persist, materialize dashboards, or fire notifications. Prior comment referenced a 'socket dispatch layer' for lifecycle management; no such layer exists.

What needs to happen:
- Parse HookEventPayload events into session_events / health_snapshots / equivalent tables (extend @nexus/db schema if needed)
- Trigger notifications on relevant events (tool_use_fail, session_stop with crash, permission_request)
- Emit to WebSocket subscribers for live dashboard updates
- Handle the 20+ event_types defined in ~/.claude/scripts/hooks/telemetry.sh (nexus currently recognizes 6, falls through to unknown for the rest)

Known event types coming in:
  Lifecycle: session_start, session_stop, session_summary, session_heartbeat, session_terminate, post_compact, pre_compact
  Agents: agent_spawn, agent_telemetry, agent_complete
  Tools: tool_use_end, tool_use_fail
  Commands: command_start, command_end, user_prompt
  Other: permission_request, teammate_idle, task_completed, instructions_loaded, config_change, worktree_create, worktree_remove, notification, hook_failure

Pointers:
  - handler: apps/agent/src/routes/hooks.ts
  - event schema in CC: ~/.claude/scripts/hooks/telemetry.sh (search 'json_event')
  - payload type: HookEventPayload interface in hooks.ts (needs expansion)

Event destination routing policy in CC (reference only, not a nexus concern):
  - All events → nexus (general event sink)
  - Curated subset → Sentry (tool_use_fail, session_stop crash, session_summary, command_end error, permission_request, hook_failure)
notes: Filed from cc /workflow:evolve follow-up on 2026-04-24. Triggering incident: nx_send calls in telemetry.sh were silent no-ops for unknown duration because nx-send.sh targeted /tmp/nexus-agent.sock which never existed. After migration to HTTP, the full event stream now reaches nexus — but handler is only ack. Extension unblocks dashboard value that the hooks pipeline was always intended to support.

[SPEC] split-core-browser-barrel
Split @nexus/core barrel to isolate Node-only modules from client code
description: The client component apps/nextjs/src/app/specs/spec-events-subscriber.tsx broke the nextjs build because @nexus/core's root barrel re-exports Node-only helpers (safeSpawn, expandTilde, parseConfig) that transitively pull node:path/node:os. Webpack cannot resolve node: schemes for the browser bundle. Fix today inlined a frame parser as a workaround (commit 6a4be9e). Proper fix: split packages/core/package.json exports to have a browser-safe subpath (e.g. @nexus/core/wire) carrying only zod schemas and types, and keep node-only helpers under the default barrel or a @nexus/core/node subpath. Without this, the next client-side consumer of a core type will trip the same build failure and silently serve stale .next/ via systemd.

title: [creds] value_encrypted stores plaintext — misleading field name implies security
description: packages/db/src/schema/credentials.ts:7 — value_encrypted column stores plaintext credentials. No encrypt/decrypt logic exists anywhere in the codebase. title: [creds] CredentialPool.lease() has TOCTOU race — concurrent leases get same credential
description: TypeScript pool.ts:60-83 reads available credentials then updates status in two separate DB operations without a transaction. Two concurrent lease requests can receive the same credential. Fix: wrap read+update in a single SQL transaction with FOR UPDATE lock.
close_reason: Addressed in TS rewrite. apps/agent/src/credentials/pool.ts:374-455 (lease method) wraps read+update in this.db.transaction() with SELECT FOR UPDATE (line 403: .for('update')). Concurrent callers serialize via Postgres row lock. Confirmed by passing test 'concurrent lease() calls: exactly one succeeds and one returns null' at apps/agent/src/credentials/credential-pool.test.ts:44-135 (bun test output: 1 pass, 3 expect() calls, 297ms). Spec encrypt-credential-storage archived 2026-04-07.

title: [creds] Non-constant-time comparison in validate_secret enables timing side-channel
description: validate_secret at crates/nexus-agent/src/http_handlers/commands.rs:113 uses == operator (non-constant-time). Attacker can use timing side-channel to brute-force X-Nexus-Secret header byte-by-byte. Fix: use subtle crate's ConstantTimeEq or ring::constant_time::verify_slices_are_equal.

title: [notification] Meeting state machine lacks transition guards
description: apps/agent/src/notifications/meeting-state.ts:1-32 — start() can be called twice, end() when not in meeting, with no error thrown. Fix: add state guards that throw on invalid transitions.

title: [creds] CredentialAccount derives Serialize without #[serde(skip)] on access_token
description: crates/nexus-core/src/credentials.rs:9-13 — CredentialAccount derives Serialize with access_token field exposed. If ever serialized to API response or log output, raw OAuth token leaks. Currently mitigated by manual projection in credentials_handler, but the type itself is latent risk. Fix: add #[serde(skip)] on access_token.
close_reason: Rust-specific concern — crates/nexus-core no longer exists (Rust→TS rewrite complete). TS equivalent uses type-level exclusion: pool.list() returns Omit<CredentialRow, 'valueEncrypted'> (apps/agent/src/credentials/pool.ts:863-872), and every route handler in apps/agent/src/routes/credentials.ts strips valueEncrypted via destructuring before response (lines 205, 401-406, 621-628). Type system provides the guarantee that #[serde(skip)] gave in Rust. Spec fix-credential-mgmt-security archived 2026-04-04.

close_reason: Verified — ReconnectBuffer at stream-manager.ts:14 with RECONNECT_BUFFER_CAPACITY, per-session lastOutput buffer records output (line 67), reconnect message type accepted at server-websocket.ts:304 with replay via stream.lastOutput.toArray(). Client can resume on reconnect without losing recent output.

title: [terminal-attach] resize message allows out-of-range values — NaN/Infinity pass type check
description: Resize handler at server.ts:333-336 checks typeof cols/rows === 'number' but does not validate ranges. Client can send cols: NaN, cols: Infinity, or rows: 999999999 — typeof NaN === 'number' passes. These are forwarded directly to pty.resize(). Fix: validate 1 <= cols <= 500 && 1 <= rows <= 300.
close_reason: Verified — server-websocket.ts:331-332 rejects resize with !Number.isFinite(cols) || !Number.isInteger(cols) || cols<1 || cols>500 (same for rows 1-300), returns JSON error frame {type: error, message: Invalid resize dimensions}. NaN and Infinity are caught by Number.isFinite.

title: [terminal-attach] Dead client via pong timeout leaves PTY running indefinitely
description: When pong timeout fires at server.ts:52-57, ws.close() triggers removeViewer() which only removes from viewers Set — it does NOT call endSession() or pty.close(). A dead client leaves the PTY process running with zero viewers indefinitely until agent restart. Fix: call endSession() when last viewer disconnects.
close_reason: Verified — PONG_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000 at server-websocket.ts:24, pongDeadlines Map at line 60, test [2.5] at server-websocket-lifecycle.test.ts:152 verifies removeViewer + endSession are called. Landed in 2026-04-04-fix-terminal-attach-security.

title: [terminal-attach] No backpressure on WebSocket output — OOM risk under fast PTY
description: PTY onData callback at stream-manager.ts:33-39 fans out to all viewers via ws.sendBinary() with bare try/catch. No maxBackpressure configured, no bufferedAmount check. Fast PTY output to slow client causes Bun internal send buffer growth without bound. Fix: add bufferedAmount check, pause PTY output when buffer exceeds threshold.
close_reason: Verified — stream-manager.ts:70-78 closes slow viewers when ws.getBufferedAmount() > 1 MB with WebSocket close code 1008 'send buffer overflow — viewer too slow'. Landed as task 1.5 of prior terminal-attach spec.

title: [session-mgmt] Session detail page missing loading.tsx and error.tsx
description: apps/nextjs/src/app/session/[id]/page.tsx:14 has no loading.tsx or error.tsx. If fetchSessionDetail throws (agent unreachable), Next.js surfaces an unhandled error page. LazyTerminalPanel has no Suspense boundary at page level. Fix: add loading.tsx + error.tsx + Suspense boundary.

title: [session-mgmt] session-manager sweepIdle never evicts ended sessions
description: sweepIdle at apps/agent/src/session-manager.ts:105-115 does not evict ended sessions — the Map grows unboundedly. Ended sessions accumulate in memory for the lifetime of the agent process. Fix: add ended session eviction with configurable TTL.

title: [session-mgmt] All integration tests skipped post-PG migration
description: sessions.test.ts at apps/agent/src/routes/sessions.test.ts:16-74 uses .skip on all tests. Zero live coverage of GET /sessions, GET /sessions/:id, status filtering, and 404 behavior after PG migration. Fix: un-skip and provide test DB fixture.

title: [session-mgmt] get/register/unregister/heartbeat missing OTel spans
description: Only start and stop session handlers have #[tracing::instrument]. handle_get_session, handle_get_sessions, handle_register_session, handle_unregister_session, and handle_heartbeat at grpc/sessions.rs:13-57 are invisible in distributed traces. Fix: add #[tracing::instrument] to all handlers.

title: [session-mgmt] handle_register_session accepts zero pid and empty fields
description: No field validation in register_session at grpc/sessions.rs:316-337 — empty cwd, zero pid, and empty session_id are silently accepted and stored. A zero pid is only caught at StopSession time. Fix: validate all required fields upfront and return InvalidArgument gRPC status.

title: [session-mgmt] SIGKILL is fire-and-forget — registry.remove() runs before process verified dead
description: handle_stop_session at grpc/sessions.rs:293-313 issues SIGKILL then sleeps 500ms then calls registry.remove() and reports success=true with 'stopped with SIGKILL' message, even if the kernel has not yet reaped the process. Fix: use waitpid with a timeout to verify death before removing from registry.
close_reason: Rust-specific — irrelevant in TS port. The TS agent (apps/agent/src/session-manager.ts) has no handle_stop_session and no SIGKILL flow. Verified: (1) routes.ts:229-262 exposes only GET /sessions, GET /sessions/:id, GET /sessions/:id/tokens, POST /session/start — no stop/kill/DELETE endpoint for sessions; (2) grep 'stop_session|stopSession|SIGKILL' under apps/agent/src returns zero hits; (3) sessions end via watcher-bridge receiving session_end CC hook events (session-manager.ts:154-169) or sweepIdle promoting to 'errored' when /proc/PID gone (session-manager.ts:230-241) or startup PID validation in init() (session-manager.ts:79-88). The only kill() in the codebase at watcher-bridge.ts:169 targets the agent's own watcher child process with a graceful-shutdown-then-force-kill pattern including proc.exitCode.then() verification (lines 164-177), which already addresses the 'verify death' concern. The Rust grpc/sessions.rs:293-313 flow referenced in the bead description does not exist in the TS rewrite.

comments.author: Leonardo Acosta
comments.text:
Discovered while fixing nx-t9wrj. Once the dashboard wiring bug was fixed, NexusAggregateClient.fetchSessions() fires correctly but every request fails with NSURLErrorDomain -1022 (App Transport Security requires secure connection) for http://100.73.182.4:7400.

Isolated runtime test (/tmp/nx-cap/atstest):
- bare swiftc binary, NO Info.plist/bundle  -> OK http=200 bytes=31728  (ATS does not apply to non-bundled executables)
- same binary in a .app bundle, unsigned, WITH NSAppTransportSecurity{NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true,NSAllowsLocalNetworking=true} -> -1022
- same, ad-hoc codesigned -> -1022
- same, launched via `open` -> -1022
- bundle WITHOUT the ATS key (baseline) -> -1022 (identical)

Conclusion: on this unsigned-dev machine the bundle Info.plist NSAppTransportSecurity exception is IGNORED — ATS engages for any .app and the exception is not honored without a properly trusted code signature (Developer ID / embedded provisioning). Adding the key to apps/swift/nexus/nexus/Info.plist was tested and did NOT work; reverted (kept nx-t9wrj scope clean).

Options for the user/architecture to decide (Breaking Changes Policy — defer to user):
1. Code-sign Nexus.app with a Developer ID so the ATS exception is honored.
2. Serve the agent over HTTPS (self-signed + pinned, or Tailscale cert) so no ATS exception is needed.
3. Verify whether a properly-signed CI/release build already honors the exception (the dev unsigned build path may be the only affected case).

Blocks the dashboard/popover from loading sessions on dev builds. Relates nx-t9wrj, nx-5ws74.

comments.author: Leonardo Acosta
comments.text:
ATS-EXCEPTION PART RESOLVED (HTTPS hardening follow-up stays OPEN).

Correction to earlier analysis: this was NOT a code-signing issue. The nexus-mac target builds with GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE semantics; the static apps/swift/nexus/nexus/Info.plist belongs to the legacy pre-XcodeGen target and was never consumed by nexus-mac — so the prior static-plist ATS edit never reached the built bundle. ATS exceptions DO work on unsigned dev builds.

FIX (apps/swift/project.yml, nexus-mac target): replaced the static `INFOPLIST_FILE: nexus/nexus/Info.plist` + flat `INFOPLIST_KEY_*` settings with an XcodeGen `info:` block (path: nexus-mac/Generated/Info.plist) whose `properties:` carry the nested NSAppTransportSecurity dict ({NSAllowsArbitraryLoads: true}) plus the preserved keys (LSUIElement: true, ATSApplicationFontsPath: Fonts, CFBundleShortVersionString, CFBundleVersion, NSHumanReadableCopyright). Flat INFOPLIST_KEY_* cannot express a nested dict, hence `info:`. NSAllowsArbitraryLoads (not NSExceptionDomains) because the endpoint is a bare Tailscale IP literal (http://100.73.182.4:7400) and the wire is already WireGuard-encrypted; internal dashboard, not App Store. `xcodegen generate` writes the generated plist + repoints pbxproj.

RUNTIME PROOF (mandatory, post-fix):
- Built bundle: `PlistBuddy -c 'Print :NSAppTransportSecurity' /Applications/Nexus.app/Contents/Info.plist` -> Dict { NSAllowsArbitraryLoads = true }; LSUIElement still true (menu-bar-only preserved).
- App stderr: ZERO -1022 / "App Transport Security" lines (prior runs had 16+). Self-test line flipped from `1 agents configured, 0 reachable, 0 sessions merged` to `1 agents configured, 1 reachable, 58 sessions merged`.
- macbook lsof: 8x ESTABLISHED TCP 100.91.88.16 -> 100.73.182.4:7400.
- homelab side (`ss -tnp` on nexus-agent pid 421006): multiple ESTABLISHED accepted FROM 100.91.88.16 (journalctl has no per-request access lines at default level; ss is the authoritative homelab-side evidence).
- Screenshot /tmp/nx-cap/dashboard-fixed.png: dashboard window renders the session list (claude rows, active/pinned); menu-bar popover also populated (cc-* CLAUDE sessions). Menu-bar status flipped "homelab unreachable" -> "homelab active".

Dashboard now actually renders sessions end-to-end. Remaining open scope on this issue: Tailscale-HTTPS hardening (serve agent over TLS so NSAllowsArbitraryLoads can be tightened/removed) — NOT implemented here per user decision.

title: stale ad_hoc sessions never get ended_at (unbounded null-pid open rows)
description: Why: nx-p71tq smoke (run 2026-05-18 against homelab Postgres via /sessions API) found 16 rows with ended_at IS NULL AND pid IS NULL. All 16 are status=stale, sessionType=ad_hoc, no cwd/tmux, age 1.4-2.7h. These are hook-origin adhoc sessions that never had a pid by design; sweepIdle correctly flips them idle->stale but NEVER sets ended_at, so they accumulate unbounded as open rows. Benign for the dashboard (stale != active, filtered out by SessionObserver.activeSessions) and does not block restart (no cwd), but violates the nx-p71tq invariant and grows without bound. Separate from nx-z66n8 (heartbeat fix, verified working). Belongs to the cleanup domain of closed proposal nx-go5gx (task 1.1 / nx-esz0i one-shot migration did not establish an ongoing reaper). What: sweepIdle (or a periodic reaper) should set ended_at when an ad_hoc session transitions to stale, OR exclude pid-less ad_hoc rows from the open-row invariant. Decide policy with Leo before implementing.
